newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK BONDS, FRNS ATTEMPT COMEBACK AFTER STEEP DROP.
newsitem.headline: GREEK BONDS, FRNS ATTEMPT COMEBACK AFTER STEEP DROP.

text.p: Greek fixed coupon bonds and floaters were attempting a comeback after suffering heavy losses due to their higher cost of carry and an unexpected auction of seven-year FRNs on June 26, dealers said.

"Bonds have recovered a bit on some institutional buying but still count losses and yields have risen 5.0 to 10 basis points after mid-session," a senior dealer at a private bank said. "FRNs have suffered the most and yields to next coupon are up an additional 5.0 to 10 basis points."
Dealers blamed the sell-off on higher interbank rates and an unexpected auction of seven-year FRNs on June 26.

"There is no fundamental reason for this mini-crisis in bonds," said a dealer. "However it shows that decisions on sensitive matters such as auctions and interest rates are being taken without taking into consideration market conditions."
The long-end of the forward curve was showing signs of easing and dealers said they expected depos to follow suit helping the recovery of bonds.
"There is money being pumped into the long-end of the market but I do not know where it is coming from," said a dealer. "It might be the finance ministry's cash reserves at the central bank."
